comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning explicitly stated it was not approving a new bar use or restaurant use at this address in 2019, requiring the space to operate as a specialty food store with no seating. This agency referral shows that when the concept changed from restaurant-accessory wine bar to grocery, Planning drew a clear line—returning to a standalone bar use will require a discretionary Conditional Use Authorizat…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 41 (beer-and-wine restaurant license) application at 5201 3rd St, 114 meters away, same NCD-BAYVIEW district and Third Street Alcohol RUD. Denied in 2017 specifically citing § 249.62 of the Third Street Alcohol RUD.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning denied a Type 41 license for a restaurant 114 meters from the subject site under § 249.62 of the Third Street Alcohol RUD. The RUD allows a Type 42 bar only with Conditional Use approval per § 249.62(a)(2)(E); this denial demonstrates that the district actively enforces alcohol restrictions and that even a restaurant beer-and-wine license faced scrutiny. A standalone Type 42 bar will fac…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Type 47 full-bar application at 5251 3rd St, 34 meters away, same NCD-BAYVIEW district. Denied in 2003 for attempting to change from a small self-service restaurant to a bar use without filing for a change-of-use building permit and conditional use authorization.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning denied a bar use at 5251 3rd St (34 meters away) because the applicant did not file a building permit for the change of use from restaurant to bar; the decision confirms that a bar (Type 47 or Type 42) is a conditional use requiring discretionary approval, not just a health referral. This is a use_decision record showing Planning actively denied a bar conversion on this block.

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Full-service restaurant and bar approved at 5251 3rd St, 34 meters away, same NCD-BAYVIEW district. Approved in 2004 as an agency referral, one year after the denial at the same address (MB0301063).

The Jazz Room's Type 48 license was later revoked by ABC, underscoring operational compliance risks on this corrido…

comparable_cases.why_comparable: Same address (5299 3rd St), Type 20 off-sale license referral approved in 2022 for the grocery store use approved in 2019. Same Third Street Alcohol RUD and NCD-BAYVIEW district.
comparable_cases.key_takeaway: Planning approved a Type 20 off-sale license (for packaged wine sales, not on-premises consumption) at this address in 2022, consistent with the grocery-store use. filing_playbook.what_to_say: If no tenant improvements are planned, state that the space is used as-built and submit only the change-of-use application. DBI will route the application to Planning; Planning will sign off because the CUA is granted. If the occupant load or occupancy group requires a Building Code change of occupancy, submit stamped plans from an architect showing compliance with ADA, exiting, and life-safety requirements. The building permit is issued after Planning and DBI review is complete.

timeline_cost.notes: This is the time to approval and government cost for the three approvals in the entitlement path: Conditional Use Authorization (120–300 days, $3,100–$15,000 per the 2026–27 fee schedule, catalog entry sf.conditional_use_authorization), health permit to operate (14–45 days, $470–$1,000, catalog entry sf.health_permit), and building permit with change of use (14–120 days for DBI review once the CUA is final, estimated $800–$15,000 depending on construction valuation, though the description states no tenant improvements so the lower end is more likely). The CUA timeline includes pre-application meeting, environmental review, 300-foot neighborhood notice, Planning Commission hearing, and the 30-day appeal period; it is the critical path. The ABC Type 42 license is not in the entitlement path because its status is insufficient information (the description does not say how the license will be obtained), but if it is a new license expect 60–120 days and $1,000–$1,600 per catalog entry ca.abc_type_42, overlapping with the CUA and running in parallel once the CUA is granted. The day range is the time to approval when these approvals are granted; it is not a time to a denial or a withdrawal. Total government cost (CUA, health, building, ABC, business registration, seller's permit, EIN, food safety manager cert, RBS training, sign permit, ASCAP/BMI licenses) is estimated at $5,500–$20,000; the operating timeline from CUA filing to opening is 6–12 months if the CUA is approved at the first hearing with no appeal.

status_definitions.allowed: Allowed: the cited records or code sections show this approval is available as of right, or already exists for this space, without a discretionary hearing.
status_definitions.further_review: Further review: the approval is obtainable only through a discretionary or multi-step review (a hearing, a referral, a licence investigation) whose result the records do not settle.
status_definitions.potential_blocker: Potential blocker: a cited rule, cap or record could stop this approval or force a change to the concept unless a specific condition is met.
status_definitions.not_permitted: Not permitted: a cited code section prohibits this use or approval at this address as the concept is described.
status_definitions.insufficient_information: Insufficient information: the records in hand do not show whether this approval is needed or obtainable; the could-not-establish section says what would settle it.

confidence_definitions.verified: Verified: stated directly by a cited record or code section that applies to this exact address, parcel or zoning district.
confidence_definitions.likely_applicable: Likely applicable: inferred from cited records of comparable cases or from a general rule; not stated for this address.
confidence_definitions.needs_confirmation: Needs confirmation: plausible but not supported by a record in hand; confirm with the agency or document named.
confidence_definitions.professional_review_required: Professional review required: depends on plans, an inspection, or legal or design judgment that public records cannot supply.

records_summary: The records show 5299 3rd St is within the Bayview Neighborhood Commercial District (NCD-BAYVIEW) and the Third Street Alcohol Restricted Use District. Under the current zoning rules a bar with an ABC Type 42 license is a conditional use here, requiring a Conditional Use Authorization. Critically, the Third Street Alcohol RUD at § 249.62(a)(2)(E) allows a new Type 42 establishment in the Bayview NCD only with Conditional Use approval. This address has recent history as Gratta Wines: in 2016 a wine bar was approved as accessory to Butchertown Gourmet restaurant, and in 2019-2020 the space transitioned to a grocery/wine-making use with a Type 20 off-sale license referral approved. Within 500 ft there is one active Type 41 license and one revoked Type 48 license; six registered food/drink businesses including four bars sit within 500 ft, signaling existing alcohol density on this block.
